original.target_description: Primary experiment on trend accuracy/social learning and partisan cues; supplied description does not specify which of multiple condition, timepoint, and political-group contrasts is targeted.

notes: Identity independently checked: title Social learning and partisan bias in the interpretation of climate trends; authors Douglas Guilbeault, Joshua Becker, Damon Centola; DOI 10.1073/pnas.1722664115; PNAS 115(39), 9714–9719 (2018). Supplied PMC canonical parse is a primary research article containing abstract, experimental design, results, methods, references and supplementary-file links, rather than an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF supplied, so the p. 3 locator cannot be resolved by page layout. Study 1 and the broad description identify the experiment but do not uniquely identify an outcome/contrast/timepoint or political subgroup. No target chosen by row order or numeric matching. Candidate comparisons: Fig. 3 improvement without cues versus party logos: printed difference 9.5 percentage points, n = 24, P = 0.01 (Wilcoxon rank sum); improvement without cues versus identity markers: n = 24, P = 0.09 (Wilcoxon rank sum). Fig. 4 final trend accuracy among conservatives, no cues versus logos: printed difference 15.7 percentage points, n = 24, P < 0.01 (Wilcoxon rank sum); no cues versus identity markers: printed difference 8.3 percentage points, n = 24, P = 0.03 (Wilcoxon rank sum). Other candidates include round-3 liberal/conservative bias in no-cue networks (n = 24, P = 0.28, Wilcoxon signed rank), logos (difference 13.7 percentage points, n = 24, P < 0.01, Wilcoxon signed rank), and identity markers (difference 12.4 percentage points, n = 24, P = 0.02, Wilcoxon signed rank). The printed percentage-point differences are not numerical Wilcoxon test statistics and were not converted. Relevant main-text tests give n and P and name Wilcoxon procedures, but do not print numerical W/U/Z statistics. Supplement is linked but is not among supplied files and was not acquired. Analytic-unit evidence: main comparisons are trial/group-level, not 2,400 recruited participants. Source explicitly states 12 observations per condition and 60 total; Fig. 4 states two subgroup observations per network and 24 per condition. Printed n = 24 is only a candidate for these contrasts, not an assigned target N. Other tests use n = 12 (within-control change), n = 48 (baseline across conditions), or n = 2,164 (individual-level baseline partisan comparison). Baseline Fig. 2 notes 122 conservatives and 114 liberals failed to enter both round-1 and round-3 responses; these exclusions cannot be assigned to a unique requested test. No analytic N sum or df inference performed. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
